result.title: Reward Basis Decomposition for Interpreting Preference Heterogeneity
result.summary: Canonical reward models specify the optimization target for AI policies, so understanding the values they encode is important for ensuring AI alignment. Existing interpretability techniques interpret reward models with a single reward head, which cannot distinguish between the values that a population shares and those that vary among individuals. We introduce Reward Basis Decomposition (RBD), which splits per-user weights into a population term and a per-user term. This yields a shared population direction and individual user directions that are analyzed separately via concept alignment and sparse autoencoder decomposition. We verify that RBD can recover artificially planted per-user directions on a synthetic control, then apply it to two real-world multi-preference datasets, PRISM and Community Alignment. In both, we find no individual-user structure, suggesting that a single direction in the reward embedding space accounts for most preferences. We verify that RBD can recover artificially planted per-user directions on a synthetic control, then apply it to two real-world multi-preference datasets, PRISM and Community Alignment. In both, we find no reliable predictive benefit from the fitted per-user terms beyond the shared population direction under our setup. Code and the synthetic dataset are available at https://github.com/RachelFreedman/RBD.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Reward Basis Decomposition，将各用户的奖励权重拆成群体项与个体项，再用概念对齐和稀疏自编码器分别解释这两部分；在合成对照上验证能恢复植入的个体方向，并在 PRISM、Community Alignment 上发现个体项几乎不能带来超出群体方向的预测收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「共享方向／个体方向」分解加 SAE 解释 latent 表示的思路，可供核查能否用于区分 LVR 内部状态中的任务共享成分与样本特有成分，以及「单一方向主导」是否对应 latent 信息坍缩；但原文无视觉推理实验。
